correctness.rationale: After dividing by one coefficient, the equal-magnitude hypothesis makes all normalized coefficients unimodular. The fixed rectangle Fourier transform is the bilinear polynomial 1+alpha z+beta w+gamma zw. With Z=alpha z, W=beta w and eta=gamma/(alpha beta), eta=1 factors into (1+Z)(1+W), giving only full row/column zeros. For eta!=1, the unit-modulus condition on W is equivalent to Z^2=eta^{-1}, yielding exactly the two unit-torus zeros (s,-s) and (-s,s). Their simultaneous membership in the two rotated root grids is equivalent to both cyclic orders being even. Explicit unimodular witnesses realize every stated count. The checker corroborates all witnesses for 2<=m,n<=40.

value.rationale: The four-point rectangle is the basic tensor support in two-dimensional finite Fourier analysis. Imposing equal coefficient magnitudes is a natural phase-only restriction, and it collapses the much richer unrestricted zero spectra to a universal parity-controlled list. The cross-phase invariant explains the mechanism and gives an all-modulus theorem with explicit witnesses, rather than a finite table or a routine parameter increment.
